video.title: How to Start an AI Automation Agency in 2026 (Step by Step)

summary: A tutorial from Mikey No Code on starting an AI automation agency in 2026 using real estate as the niche. He builds three Base44 Super Agents (speed-to-lead follow-up, inquiry triage/scoring, weekly executive reporting), then packages them as a 'Real Estate Growth Suite' with a setup fee plus monthly retainer. He covers cold outreach with a Loom demo and a free 15-minute audit, discovery calls, contracts, a 48-hour onboarding, case studies, raising prices, and hiring an operator after $5-10k MRR. The video is promotional for his Base44 master class and contains no first-hand revenue evidence; prices are recommendations.

ideas.name: Niche AI automation agency for real estate brokerages (Real Estate Growth Suite)
ideas.one_liner: Sell brokerages a package of three AI agents (instant lead follow-up, inquiry triage, weekly reporting) built on Base44 for a setup fee plus monthly retainer.
ideas.business_model: One-off setup fee plus monthly retainer per office/team
ideas.customer: Real estate brokerages, property groups and teams; owner, managing broker or operations lead
ideas.problem: Slow lead response, poor inquiry qualification, and manual weekly reporting cause lost commissions and wasted staff time.
ideas.offer: Real Estate Growth Suite: speed-to-lead follow-up agent (personalised reply within ~120 seconds, 48h and 96h follow-ups), property inquiry triage agent (1-10 urgency score, alerts for hot leads, Google Sheet log for the rest), and weekly executive reporting agent (Sunday 8pm). Ready in 7-10 business days.

pricing.model: Setup fee plus monthly retainer; no hourly billing

Setup fee range for first few clients
Setup fee once proof/case study exists
Typical real estate retainer per office/team

pricing.notes: Requires full setup fee before account configuration begins. Retainer covers monitoring, prompt updates, model updates, API/connection fixes and small additions. Advises against charging ~$100 or working free.

acquisition_channels.details: Direct email to the owner/managing broker/operations lead (not info@ addresses) with a problem-solution-result message and a 2-3 minute Loom demo video; CTA is a free 15-minute lead flow and operations audit.

quote.text: you don't need a large ad budget or say a complicated funnel to land your first few clients. For an early stage agency, direct outreach is usually the better route.
quote.speaker: Mikey

acquisition_channels.details: LinkedIn outreach to managing brokers, agency owners and other decision makers using the same specific message.
After ~30 days, turn results into a case study with real numbers (response time, hours saved, extra showings) to use in later outreach and shorten the sales cycle.

ideas.delivery: Operator clones three production-tested Base44 Super Agent templates per client, updates system prompts (company name, service area, hours, tone, rules), connects the client's Gmail/Google Workspace/CRM via OAuth through a secure credentials link, runs end-to-end validation tests with simulated leads, then goes live. Standard 48-hour onboarding; later deployments take hours. Ongoing monitoring and prompt/connection maintenance under the retainer. Later a junior operator is hired using documented SOPs.
unit_economics_claims: Agency target of 5-10 retainer clients in one niche before expanding
MRR of $5,000-$10,000 is the trigger to hire an operator
Illustrative case study: response time 4 hours to 85 seconds, 18 hours saved weekly, 3 extra showings in month one
ideas.startup_cost: not stated (Base44 subscription cost not given; mostly the operator's time)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Plan: first month to choose niche, build demos and start outreach and close the first client; deployment and case study in month two.

acquisition.how: Cold email to limited-company brokerages is legal in the UK and can be agent-assisted for list building and drafting, but the pitch, Loom demo, audit call and closing need a human. LinkedIn DMs and sole-trader emails run into PECR.

onboarding.how: Template cloning, credential collection links and validation tests are routine; a human checks scope, contract and client-specific rules.

delivery.how: Once live the Base44 agents run unattended (follow-ups, scoring, weekly report); setup per client needs occasional human approval and testing.

billing.how: Setup fee plus monthly retainer can be invoiced and collected automatically via Stripe or similar; the video does not detail billing.

support.how: Retainer work such as expired connections, model changes and prompt tweaks needs monitoring and human judgement, though agents can triage tickets.

uk_applicability.notes: The model works in the UK with UK estate agents using Rightmove/Zoopla enquiries instead of Zillow/MLS. Outreach must respect PECR (cold email to limited companies OK, sole traders need care), GDPR for lead data processing, and prices in GBP. Commission per sale is lower in the UK, so ROI framing differs. Dependence on Base44 is a platform risk.

risks: Heavy dependence on Base44 platform and model behaviour
Scope creep and unclear expectations if the offer is vague
Connections can expire and models change, creating ongoing maintenance
Pricing and results are unverified; the video is a promo for a course
Fierce competition from other AI agency pitches
GDPR/PECR exposure when processing lead data and doing outreach in the UK

tactics.name: Niche-specific agency positioning
steps: Pick one industry you understand (here real estate)
Use industry language in outreach (speed to lead, MLS, pre-approval, commissions)
Reuse templates and case studies across clients
Stay in the niche until 5-10 retainer clients before expanding

quote.text: positioning yourself as the AI person for every type of business, well, that forces you to create a different offer for every prospect.
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: Demo-led cold outreach with free audit
steps: Build three working demo agents first
Record a 2-3 minute Loom of lead arriving, fast reply, scoring and report
Email owner/managing broker directly: problem, system, measurable result
Offer a free 15-minute lead flow and operations audit rather than asking for $2,500
Avoid jargon like LLM orchestration or vector databases
Avoid generic info@ addresses

quote.text: the strongest asset that you can bring into this outreach is a short recorded walkthrough of the demo agent.
quote.speaker: Mikey

tactics.name: Discovery call then single bundled package
steps: Ask them to walk through what happens the minute a lead comes in at 8pm
Ask hours per week spent sorting unqualified inquiries
Ask how weekly follow-up performance is tracked
Present all three agents as one package, not a menu
Document scope in a contract with max three active agents and full setup fee before configuration

tactics.name: Standardised 48-hour onboarding
steps: Send secure OAuth credentials collection link, never passwords by email
Clone the three production-tested templates in Base44
Update prompts with company name, service area, hours, tone, rules
Replace demo connections with client's live accounts
Run end-to-end validation with simulated leads
Review with client then go live

tactics.name: Case study to raise prices
steps: Run the system 30 days
Capture response time, hours saved, extra showings
Use the case study in outreach
Raise setup fee from ~$1,500 to $3,500+

tactics.name: Test agents with simulated leads before going live
steps: Run a sample inquiry (name, property, budget) through the agent
Test two opposite leads to check scoring separation
Run a sample week of numbers for the report
Fix wording and criteria before touching a live inbox

warnings.warning: Do not undercharge for the first deal; very low prices attract clients expecting unlimited revisions.

quote.text: avoid offering the entire setup for a hundred bucks or working for free out of desperation
quote.speaker: Mikey

warnings.warning: Do not start client-specific work on a verbal agreement; document scope and payment terms first.
Promising ten automations creates scope creep and more things that can break; start with two or three.
Do not expand to a new niche too early.
Never ask clients to send passwords via email or chat; use OAuth.
Do not ask for a $2,500 setup fee in the first cold message.

lessons.lesson: Sell a specific expensive problem (slow lead response) with measurable ROI, not AI technology.

quote.text: what you do need is one expensive, repetitive problem inside a business and a system that fixes it automatically.
quote.speaker: Mikey

lessons.lesson: Specialising in one niche makes outreach more credible and lets templates, case studies and processes be reused.
Setup fee plus retainer beats hourly billing because efficiency raises rather than lowers your earnings.
Lead with the strongest-ROI demo (speed to lead) in sales conversations.
Weekly reporting makes the retainer's value visible and reduces churn risk.
Document every procedure so delivery can be handed to a junior operator and the founder can focus on sales.
Productised, cloned templates make marginal delivery cost per client drop dramatically.
Test with simulated inputs before connecting to live client systems.
Treat low-code AI agent platforms as a dependency; the defensible value is niche knowledge, sales and process rather than the tool.

evidence_quality.rationale: Tutorial with no first-hand client revenue or results; prices and case-study figures are recommendations or hypotheticals. The build walkthrough is concrete, but the business claims are unverified and the video is promotional.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Promotes his Base44 master class (normally $499, offered free via link) and the Base44 platform.
